That leaves one last lead:
the cloakroom attendant, Prokhorov.
437:
But we couldn't check it.
Prokhorov didn't come to the meeting.
438:
He must suspect something.
He quit his job and hasn't been home.
440:
You have our apologies and deepest thanks.
Take off the wig, wash away the tattoos,
441:
go home and celebrate the New Year.
Thank you so much.
- What about my people?
442:
We'll return your charges
to prison today.
443:
If you find the cloakroom attendant,
might you need us again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you,
but Bely—the real Docent—
escaped from prison today.
445:
Unbelievable, but true.
It isn't safe for you to look like him.
446:
Could we wait until tomorrow?
It is New Year's, and they did try
in their own way.
447:
We're outside the city.
It's unlikely Docent could find us.
448:
All right, but don't leave the house!
We forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife.
Here's her reply, addressed to him.
450:
- You'll have lunch with us on New Year's Day?
- We promise!
451:
It's a shame. Such a nice woman,
and her father's a fence and a profiteer.
452:
What's all this shouting?
Who said you could go out?
- He's back. The bad man.
454:
A new year has begun. I hope
everything changes for you this year.
455:
Anything can happen, but remember:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you.
I'll make sure I find you.
457:
- And now... just a moment...
- Where's he going?
458:
Who knows? You can't make sense
of him anymore.
459:
What's not to understand? He says
he'll find us wherever we go
and slit our throats.
461:
They say he ran a razor across Speckle's
throat—snick, goodbye.
- He's gone completely savage, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to visit?
Father Frost, with presents for you!
463:
- Come here, Fedya. - What did I do?
- Come on. Wear these slippers in good health.
464:
- What do I need slippers for?
I haven't even got a home.
- You will. Your life's ahead of you.
465:
- They'll be useful in prison meanwhile.
- You always have to jinx things.
466:
This is for you, Vasya.
And this is yours, Gavrila Petrovich.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- And this is yours too.
469: It's sour. It's no fun without vodka.
470:
- Must you get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could sit and have
a heart-to-heart talk.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor. I'm not here
for a heart-to-heart.
- We could play a game.
473:
Listen to him! You think I'm a sucker?
You've got nine aces in your deck.
474: It doesn't have to be cards.
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say “Moscow.”
476:
You take the last letter, W,
and say “Warsaw.”
Then you say “Washington.” See?
477:
Now you, Fedya.
Name a city beginning with N.
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- All right. So yours begins with A.
- Dzhambul. - Why Dzhambul?
480:
Because it's warm there.
My home is there. My mother too.
481:
Let's try another game. I'll go out,
you hide something, and I'll find it.
482:
- You could try finding our helmet.
- Quiet.
483:
- We'll hide it and he'll peek through a hole?
- Then you go out and hide it.
484:
You make sure I don't peek.
Why me? Anything comes up,
it's always Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your maw open,
you little rascal!
- Maw, maw...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- Did you have a mom and dad?
- I did.
488:
Why are you so mean?
Why are you like a dog?
490:
- He came on his own.
- Oh, you're here too.
491:
I tried your place,
but I could tell it was staked out.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Keep walking.
495:
- I'm sorry we called you out for nothing, doctor.
- It's all right.
496:
Give him valerian drops and warm tea,
and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499:
“Dear Dad, hello. We found out
you're in prison
500:
and were very happy,
because we thought you were dead.”
501:
What bastard told that little boy
his father's a crook?
502:
“Mom was happy too. When your letter
came, she cried all day.
503:
Before that, she'd said
you were a test pilot.”
504: More like a pilot of raids.
505:
“Anyway, I'm glad you're alive,
because Mom says
506:
you're a good man
but weak-willed.”
507:
Exactly! So weak-willed, he nicked
our money and blamed the taxi driver.
508:
Scarper! I'll knock off your horns,
you rotten radish!
510:
You should be ashamed! You're forty.
Half your lives are over.
511:
What have you done?
What do you have now? What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it's too late.
That's my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we need to get out.
That woman doctor will tell the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I ran my razor across her throat.
515:
She's down the well.
Go look if you like.
516: What was my sentence? One year.
517: How much for the escape? Three!
518:
The nursery and the apartment?
Let's say ten!
520:
And for a measly fourteen years,
I must put up with this viper?
521:
Who put an old woman down a well?
Do what you want. I'm going to the police.
522: Go ahead! He won't touch you.
523:
What about you? Will you put up
with him until he kills you?
524:
Vasya, the other day I told him
I had a cold, and he...
525:
Enough about your cold already.
Come here.
527:
- What are you doing?
- Cleaning the rug.
528:
Well, comrades, the show's over.
First, I'll take this off.
530:
Once I've done my time, that's it.
I'll go straight! Get a job.
531:
- Doing what?
- Watchman on my old collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I could clear snow, lay bricks,
or be a translator. I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought the hat too!
Docent's a crook.
534:
- Plenty of crooks, only one hat.
- They'd reduce our sentences for the helmet.
535:
Where did he put it?
We checked everywhere.
536:
Crook! I told you I had a cold,
and all you said was “Maw, maw!”
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing weather!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they caught us. Remember?
He said he was fishing, and I should dive.
539:
- Wait. What did he say about fishing?
- “I'm fishing through a hole in the ice.
540:
Squint, can you swim?”
- He hid the helmet in that ice hole!
541:
That's it! I remember, the bad man!
The hole's at Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you speak up, you lout?
You could've left a note before hanging yourself!
- Let's go.
543:
- What about him?
- Let them collect him. I'm not carrying
a great lump like that. Come on!
545:
- There's nothing down there.
- It's at the bottom. Someone has to dive.
546:
Why me? Whenever there's a job,
it's always Squint. Tell him to go himself, Vasya.
547:
I can't! It's cold.
I'll get sick.
548:
- Just now you were hanging yourself,
and now you're afraid of catching a cold!
- Greetings, sports fans!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551:
I'd do you in,
but I haven't got the time!
552:
Now there are two of them.
And another at the country house.
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
